narr: An upper-level low pressure system just off the California Coast and the subtropical high pressure system over the southern Plains led to strong southerly flow across southern California. This helped transport higher moisture content northward with precipitable water values reaching above 1.5. This led to moderate to strong instability across southeast California with MLCAPE values of approximately 1500-2000 J/KG. A thunderstorm complex developed across western portions of Joshua Tree National Park near Highway 177 and persisted for several hours as upslope flow led to training. Between 4-6 inches of rain fell according to doppler radar estimates, leading to overflowing washes. These washes intersect Highway 177 and thus led to the flooding, forcing the closure.
ev: Highway 177 north of Desert Center closed due to significant flooding between approximately Mile Markers 13 to 18. No damages or injuries were reported.
lsr: SR-177 closed due to significant flooding along the highway between approximately Mile Markers 13 to 18.
